[What I offer]{.eyebrow}

Six ways I work with research groups, hospitals, policy bodies and health-tech teams. Each entry says what it is, who it is for, and what you get back. If your problem sits between two of these, that is normal — say so and we will scope it.

::: {.offers}

:::: {.offer #study-design}
[01]{.offer__num}

::: {.offer__body}
### Study & survey design

Sample size, choice of measures, and the design decisions that determine whether the data can answer the question at all.

[For: anyone about to collect data — a trial, a cohort, a survey, an audit.]{.who}

What you get back: a design that is analysable later and avoids the errors that only surface once collection is finished.
:::
::::

:::: {.offer #psychometrics}
[02]{.offer__num}

::: {.offer__body}
### Instrument validation & psychometrics

Scale development and evaluation: factor structure, reliability, and measurement invariance across groups or time.

[For: teams building or adopting a questionnaire, index or rating scale.]{.who}

What you get back: evidence that your instrument measures what you claim, and holds up across the groups you compare.
:::
::::

:::: {.offer #analysis}
[03]{.offer__num}

::: {.offer__body}
### Statistical analysis & modelling

Multilevel, survival and Bayesian modelling, and causal inference for observational data.

[For: researchers and organisations with data in hand and a decision to make.]{.who}

What you get back: a defensible analysis, reproducible code, and a plain account of what it does and does not support.
:::
::::

:::: {.offer #simulation}
[04]{.offer__num}

::: {.offer__body}
### Simulation & health economics

Patient-flow and capacity modelling, agent-based simulation, and cost-effectiveness analysis.

[For: managers and policy bodies weighing a change before committing to it.]{.who}

What you get back: a model of the trade-off, with the uncertainty made explicit rather than hidden.
:::
::::

:::: {.offer #review}
[05]{.offer__num}

::: {.offer__body}
### Statistical review & second opinion

An independent read of an analysis — before submission, or after a reviewer has taken it apart.

[For: authors, editors, and teams who need a check they can trust.]{.who}

What you get back: a clear judgement on what is sound, what is not, and what to fix first.
:::
::::

:::: {.offer #training}
[06]{.offer__num}

::: {.offer__body}
### Training

Research methods and applied statistics taught to clinical and research teams, pitched at the room.

[For: departments who want to raise the floor, not just outsource the analysis.]{.who}

What you get back: a session or short series built around your own data and questions.
:::
::::

:::

## How it works

1. **Initial call.** A short, no-obligation conversation to understand the problem and whether I am the right person for it.
2. **Scoped proposal.** A written scope: the question, the approach, the deliverable, and the timeline.
3. **Agreed deliverable.** The work, delivered as agreed — analysis, report, model, or review.

I work as a registered self-employed practitioner in Belgium and invoice accordingly.

Rates are discussed at the scoping call, once the work is clear.
